blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) is a blood clot in a vein, usually in the leg.
DVT can be dangerous.
Get medical help as soon as possible if you think you have DVT.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Symptoms of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: Symptoms of DVT (deep vein thrombosis) in the leg include:

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Symptoms of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: throbbing pain in 1 leg (rarely both legs), usually in the calf or thigh

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Symptoms of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: swelling in 1 leg (rarely both legs)

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Symptoms of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: red, blue or darkened skin around the painful area – this may be harder to see on brown or black skin

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Symptoms of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: swollen veins

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Symptoms of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: These symptoms can sometimes happen in your arm if that's where the blood clot is.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Symptoms of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: Sometimes the only symptom you may have is pain in your lower tummy.
This is a symptom of pelvic vein thrombosis, but this is rare.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you think you have DVT (deep vein thrombosis)

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: You can call 111 or get help from 111 online.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: If you're pregnant you can also call an early pregnancy unit (if you're less than 20 weeks) or your maternity unit, if you have the phone number.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: You have symptoms of DVT (deep vein thrombosis), such as pain and swelling, and:

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: feel short of breath

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: have chest pain

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: DVT can be very serious because blood clots can travel to your lungs.
This is called a pulmonary embolism.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: A pulmonary embolism can be life-threatening and needs treatment straight away.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Do not drive to A&E. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 and ask for an ambulance.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Bring any medicines you take with you.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: A DVT (deep vein thrombosis) is more likely to happen if you:

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: are aged over 60

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: are living with overweight or obesity

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: smoke

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: have had DVT before

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: take HRT

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: take the combined contraceptive pill or use contraception that contains oestrogen, such as the patch or vaginal ring

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: have cancer or heart failure

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: have varicose veins

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: have thrombophilia – a condition where your blood clots more easily

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: have inflammatory bowel disease or vasculitis

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: have thoracic outlet syndrome – a condition that can affect blood flow to your arm

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: There are also some times when you have a higher chance of getting DVT.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: These include when you:

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: are staying in or recently left hospital – especially if you cannot move around much

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: are having, or have had, surgery

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: have a medical device implanted, such as a pacemaker

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: are confined to bed for 3 days or more

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: go on a long journey (more than 4 hours) by plane, car or train

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: are pregnant or if you've had a baby in the previous 6 weeks

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: are pregnant and have had DVT before

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: are dehydrated

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Who is more likely to get DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: Sometimes DVT can happen for no obvious reason.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How DVT (deep vein thrombosis) is diagnosed
s: If a doctor thinks you have DVT (deep vein thrombosis), you should be referred to hospital within 24 hours for an ultrasound scan.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How DVT (deep vein thrombosis) is diagnosed
s: The scan shows whether blood is flowing normally through the vein.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Treatment of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) is treated with blood-thinning medicines.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Treatment of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: You'll usually need to take blood-thinning medicines, such as rivaroxaban, for at least 3 months to reduce your risk of getting another blood clot.
These medicines are usually taken as tablets.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Treatment of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: If you get a DVT when you're pregnant, you'll usually need blood-thinning injections for the rest of your pregnancy and until your baby is 6 weeks old.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Treatment of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: You may also need other treatments if a condition has caused your DVT.
If the cause of your DVT is not clear, you may need further tests to find out what caused it.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Recovery from DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: There are things you can do to help you recover from DVT (deep vein thrombosis).

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Recovery from DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: After you leave hospital, you'll be encouraged to:

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Recovery from DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: stay active – walk regularly if you can

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Recovery from DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: keep your affected leg raised when you're sitting

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Recovery from DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: delay any flights or long journeys until at least 2 weeks after you start taking blood-thinning medicine

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis)
s: There are things you can do to lower your chance of getting DVT (deep vein thrombosis).

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Do stay a healthy weight stay active – taking regular walks can help drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration – DVT is more likely if you're dehydrated Don't
s: do not sit still for long periods of time – get up and move around every hour or so

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Do stay a healthy weight stay active – taking regular walks can help drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration – DVT is more likely if you're dehydrated Don't
s: do not smoke

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Do stay a healthy weight stay active – taking regular walks can help drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration – DVT is more likely if you're dehydrated Don't
s: do not drink lots of alcohol

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going on a long journey
s: If you're travelling for 4 hours or more by plane, train or car, there are things you can do during the journey to lower your chances of getting DVT.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going on a long journey
s: These include:

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going on a long journey
s: wearing loose clothing

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going on a long journey
s: drinking plenty of water

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going on a long journey
s: avoiding alcohol

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going on a long journey
s: walking around when possible

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going into hospital
s: If you go into hospital, your healthcare team should check if there's a higher chance you'll get DVT.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going into hospital
s: If they think you're more likely to get DVT, you may be given treatment to prevent it, such as medicine.
You may also be given compression stockings (knee-high elastic socks that help your blood circulation) while you're in hospital.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going into hospital
s: Sometimes you may continue treatment to prevent DVT after you leave hospital, for example, if you've had surgery, because a blood clot can happen weeks later.

blocks.path: DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > How to prevent DVT (deep vein thrombosis) > Going into hospital
s: You can also help reduce your risk of DVT while you're in hospital by staying active and walking around if you can.
